content.comment_body: Does anyone know how to completely turn off the display? I tried adding various texts, even an entirely blank one, but the screen still emits an orange glow and continues to show the date.

It sometimes feels like this is way more complicated than expected. If you use a shift register and want to shift a sequence like '1-0-1-0-1-0' with the cursor key, it doesn't always work. When no message is active and you press ESC, you get the [product_name] menu instead. You'll need a different approach. For example, if an input replaces the cursor key, shifting does work, but then you face another issue: on every second clock cycle, two shift register bits are active, so two messages are displayed, and the one with higher priority appears (such as B024). Since one of the three shift register bits is always on, the indicator for the background color stays active.
Shift registers can be tricky. I took one of the examples you posted, added another position, and then it stopped working as expected. I'll keep trying to solve it. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue discussed is the inability to fully switch off or deactivate the display or backlight of the [product_name] device. User attempts using blank text or configuration changes haven't worked, and using shift registers brings further difficulties such as priority conflicts and input logic, leading to unexpected display behaviors and ongoing screen illumination.
analysis.user_expectations: User wants to be able to configure the system so the screen/backlight is completely off, so no light or display remains visible.
pain_keywords: inability to fully turn off display
